messages.subject: combining a stacked bar plot with a normal bar plot
parts:
Hi,


Is there a way to combine a stacked bar plot together with a normal bar. I have a df with four columns. 
I would like to put three of them stacked on top of each other in one bar and the fourth one on a second bar next to it in a group-wise manner. 

I am using the melt command to melt the three to stack into one melted data frame, but i can't find out how to combine to aes() objects into the same plot.

is it possible at all?

thanks

Assa

my code for the stacked plot with the three columns

> rownames(output) <- name.vector

> colnames(output) <- c("total", "A", "B", "C")

> output

      total              A           B        C

S1 37031624       32983885     2528032  1519707

S2 31447403       28041515     2106630  1299258

S3 48318274       43184390     3277553  1856331

S4 43217950       38786317     2882760  1548873

S5 38883095       34897837     2514010  1471248

S6 41266768       37043631     2695805  1527332

S7 41836195       37426964     2798669  1610562

S8 43448424       38886827     2962280  1599317

> df.melt <- melt(output[,c("A", "B", "C")],id.vars = rownames(output))

> ggplot(df.melt, aes(x = X1, y = value,fill=X2)) + 

+   geom_bar(stat='identity', colour="black") +

+   scale_fill_manual(values=c("black", "grey", "white"))

copy and paste it to the command line.

messages.subject: Re: combining a stacked bar plot with a normal bar plot
parts:
>Hi Ron, thank you for the answer. But no this is not always the case.
>Maybe the column header is a bit confusing. But the three columns might
>be results after filtering and the total is the number without the
>filtering. This is why I would like
> to add the one "total" column to the stacked column of the results.

dput(output) would have allowed me to easily use your example data.
Instead I've crudely simulated some of my own.

This might help you get going:

# Create some simulated data a bit like yours
output <- data.frame(A=rpois(8,1000),B=rpois(8,1100),
C=rpois(8,1200),total=rpois(8,3300),
row=paste0("S",1:8),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

library(reshape2)
df.melt <- melt(output,id.var="row")
# Specify which values belong to the stacked or total column
df.melt$coltype <- ifelse(df.melt$variable=="total","total","pile")
df.melt$x<-paste(df.melt$row,df.melt$coltype,sep=".")

ggplot(df.melt)+
geom_bar( aes( x=paste(row,coltype,sep="."), y=value,
group=coltype, fill=variable), stat="identity" )


Regards,
Ron.
